Civic Leadership Awards 
The UMass Dartmouth Civic Leadership Awards recognize the civic engagement contributions of our students, faculty, 
and community members. This year’s recipients were: 
Community Member Civic Leadership Award 
Fr. Sr. Rob Nemkovich,   Blessed Trinity Parish 
Fr. Sr. Rob Nemkovich, is the pastor of Blessed Trinity Church in Fall River, MA, 
chaplain for the Fall River Police Department, and Parish Administrator of Holy 
Cross Parish in Central Falls, RI. He serves in numerous national and diocesan 
leadership roles within the Polish National Catholic Church and has demonstrated 
an unwavering commitment to service and community by bringing together faith, 
public safety, and community organizations to address the root causes of gun 
violence, homelessness, food insecurity, addiction, mental health challenges, and 
social isolation. Through his long standing compassionate leadership, he has built 
lasting partnerships and created sustainable programs that have improved the 
lives of individuals and families throughout the Greater Fall River community. 
Faculty Civic Leadership Award 
Ziddi Msangi,   Design 
Ziddi Msangi is a Design professor who has devoted his career to education and the 
development of informed citizens. He believes effective learning occurs through 
active engagement, therefore his pedagogical approach prioritizes experiential 
learning, collaborative activities, and inclusive design. Professor Msangi joined 
the Community Engaged Teaching + Learning Faculty Fellow Program in 2009 and 
was nominated in recognition of his successful establishment of partnerships that 
integrated community-engaged learning projects into the curriculum. One such 
partnership, with Allens Pond Wildlife Sanctuary in Dartmouth, MA, remains active 
to this day. Additional collaborations include the Boys and Girls Club in Fall River, 
the New Bedford Art Museum, and the Cambodian Community of Fall River (CCFR). 
Student Civic Leadership Award 
Chelsee Rennie   ‘26,   Law + Public Policy 
Chelsee Rennie, from Portland, Oregon, graduated in 2026 with a Juris Doctorate 
from UMass Law and a Master of Public Policy from UMass Dartmouth. She served 
on the Graduate Student Senate, as Vice President of Non-Traditional Affairs for 
the Student Bar Association, and held executive board positions with If/When/How: 
Lawyers for Reproductive Freedom, the First Generation Law Student Association, 
the Legal Association Against Sexual Exploitation, and the National Lawyers Guild. 
Chelsee was the Lead Legal Mentor for the Discovering Justice After-School Mock 
Trial team at Normandin Middle School, founded Beyond the Bar, interned with 
State Senator Dylan Fernandes, and helped establish a free immigration clinic in 
partnership with the Community Economic Development Center (CEDC).
